solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Travel document shown by directors in Golf? I don't know

parts.note: a company's directors together form its board
G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in a quiz, saying pass means you don't know the answer

explanation.surface: A travel document is being shown off by company directors playing golf, and someone shrugs.
explanation.walkthrough: A quizmaster's "pass" is what a contestant says instead of "I don't know".
explanation.definitionFit: A boarding pass is the card a passenger must show to get onto a plane, a standard piece of travel paperwork.

clue.text: Exploded item of statuary incorporating King

indicators.note: the statue word takes the king's letter into its body

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: A statue of a king blew apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has burst has blown open violently, much as an explosion does.

clue.text: A TV and broadcast age offering benefit

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Owning a television in a broadcasting age has its upside.
explanation.walkthrough: "Broadcast" sits naturally beside TV, but here it means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a favourable circumstance, a synonym for benefit as a noun.

clue.text: Treatment of teeth: repositioned in head gently, with minimum of effort

indicators.note: the letters are moved into different positions, signalling a rearrangement
the least possible part of the word effort is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dentist's instructions: brush teeth gently, without much effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental hygiene is the routine care of teeth and gums, such as brushing and flossing.

clue.text: Subtlety? Good attempt, but not right

parts.note: nice is a mild word for good

indicators.note: the right letter is not allowed to stay, so it is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: R, as in R for right

explanation.surface: Praising a near miss: nice try, but it wasn't right.
explanation.walkthrough: "Nice try" is the consolation for a near miss, which makes the surface natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or distinction, so a subtlety.

clue.text: Various items — a harp, a praline — scattered around

indicators.note: the letters are strewn about and come back in another order

explanation.surface: A harp and a sweet lie strewn about with other clutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphernalia means miscellaneous belongings or equipment, an assortment of odds and ends.

clue.text: Father supporting Southern resort

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad is paying for a holiday at a southern resort.
explanation.walkthrough: "Supporting" suggests paying for; in a down answer it means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs where people go for health and leisure, a kind of resort.

clue.text: Iron company avoiding settlement is a criminal act

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the settlement word steers clear of the company letters, which are taken out

parts.note: a colony is a settlement established in a new territory

explanation.surface: A steel firm's refusal to pay a settlement is called a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: "Settlement" reads as a legal payout; it is a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious crime in law, so it is an offence of the gravest class.

clue.text: Bird's name given to music party

parts.note: a rave is a large party with dance music

explanation.surface: A bird's name gets borrowed for a music party.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black crow-family bird.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise with herb appearing in floral arrangement

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh'

explanation.surface: Someone gasps to find a herb tucked into a bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsage is a small bunch of flowers worn pinned to a dress or wrist.

clue.text: Last characters in text indicate uncertain number

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The end of a message suggests the figure is in doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten is a cardinal number, one more than nine.

clue.text: A new suggestion regarding opening course

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion
as to means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fresh proposal about how to start something.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables served before the main meal.

clue.text: America turned dirty on a continuing basis

indicators.note: the abbreviation for America is turned round, read backwards

explanation.surface: America went bad and stayed that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained effort is kept up without interruption, so it is ongoing or continuous.

clue.text: Fine place for mascara that's overly decorative

parts.note: mascara is brushed onto the eyelashes

explanation.surface: Mascara applied to the lashes looks a bit much.
explanation.walkthrough: F for fine is a pencil-grade abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Flash is informal for showy or ostentatious, as in a flash car.

clue.text: Celebration, after loss of heart, encourages and cheers

indicators.note: the word for encourages loses its central letter

parts.note: fires as in fires up, stirs enthusiasm
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: After a bout of despondency, a party lifts everyone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: "Loss of heart" reads as low morale but means the middle letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive occasion, originally a Spanish religious holiday.

clue.text: Attempt meeting of bridge opponents, for example

parts.note: East and South sit as opponents at the bridge table
say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: An effort to bring two rival bridge players together, say.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play East-West, so E and S are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is a formal word meaning to try it.

clue.text: Inclines to have millions invested in race venue

indicators.note: the millions letter is placed inside the word for inclines

explanation.surface: Someone tends to sink millions into a motor-racing circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Mans is the French town that hosts the famous 24-hour sports car race.

clue.text: Most of each part of the golf-course staying fresh

indicators.note: the word for each loses its last letter

parts.note: the green is the area around the hole

explanation.surface: Nearly every bit of the golf course keeps fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes plants that keep leaves all year, and figuratively things that never grow stale.

clue.text: An opening for trainee soldier

indicators.note: the opening of the word trainee is its first letter

explanation.surface: A vacancy for an army recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: "Trainee soldier" looks like one unit, but the definition is soldier alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier ant is the large-jawed caste that defends a colony, so an ant can be a soldier.

clue.text: Singer partly prone to getting upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards
only part of these words is used, so the answer is hidden inside them

explanation.surface: A singer who is somewhat inclined to get upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a man who sings in the high male voice range.

clue.text: Thin material turned fat, horribly fat, with infusion of energy

indicators.note: the first fat is turned round and read backwards
energy's letter is steeped into the jumbled letters
the second fat is horribly mangled, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Fabric that went fat, horribly so, after an energy boost.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous fabric of silk or synthetic fibre used for dresses.

clue.text: Viral infection was airborne, according to radio report

indicators.note: what is heard over the radio is the sound, not the spelling

explanation.surface: A radio bulletin says a virus spread through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu, short for influenza, is a contagious illness caused by a virus.

clue.text: Material business in place before November

indicators.note: the business word is set ahead of the November letter

parts.note: a line is a line of business or trade

explanation.surface: A cloth trade set up before winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is cloth woven from flax fibres.

clue.text: Australian monarch getting defamation

parts.note: a queen is a reigning monarch

explanation.surface: An Australian royal is the target of libellous talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A Queenslander is someone from Queensland, the north-eastern state of Australia.
